task_contract.anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after routing and input preparation, whose own body constructs the target observable value rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the sink.

runtime_boundary.event_plane: DOM CustomEvent on the main document

evidence: The DevTools-visible JavaScript corpus is a single obfuscated bundle and no source map is exposed to the agent.
The observable field name is assembled from character-code arrays at the sink, so literal field search is not sufficient.
The browser capability surface is collected only after a preflight, hardened profile selection, explicit consent, arm action and final commit gate have all succeeded.
The active function is surrounded by high-similarity ticket reducers and 44 off-chain decoy modules.

The target path crosses delegated event handling, action-table routing, preflight state mutation, consent/profile gating, arm-state mutation, final gate verification, form normalization, environment-surface collection, asynchronous scheduling, local event dispatch, middleware, state-machine transit calculation and sink wrapping.
Submit-time debug and info decoys emit ticket-like shadow keys that do not feed the requested fingerprint field.
The same core module retains legacy reducer factories that resemble the target constructor but do not construct the browser fingerprint.
Browser surface fields are collected only after the multi-action gate opens, then encoded after Promise, microtask, timer, animation-frame, MutationObserver and CustomEvent boundaries.
The final sink receives an already encoded value under a dynamically reconstructed field name.
Route action context surrounds the fingerprint construction, while form-derived transit stays outside the final browser-surface digest.

behavior_category.subtype: stable browser capability and viewport digest
behavior_category.reason: The observable value is derived from navigator, screen, viewport, media-query and locale/timezone browser surface fields rather than from a request signature, byte array transform, UI state code or request payload rewrite.

near_categories.why_not: The output has no request proof or token semantics and no network request is made.
The form and route state are path context; the target value is anchored by browser capability collection and digest construction.
No request body is emitted or rewritten.
